I remember seeing something like this. But it was on an old version. 

A new emby/plex library wouldn't scan completely. 

I think  _ls -R_ had better results.
ls -l doesn't see all the directories when viewed via the cache mount, but does when doing it via the non-cached mount. Simply using `ls -l `displays a different number of directories

Could the new files be new ones added outside the cache remote? 
The parent directory would cache the listing when you first execute it for `--cache-info-age` time. After that time passes, the cached listing of the parent folder is evicted and a new listing would get the data from the cloud provider.
If you purge the cache and run again, are they still not displayed?

If they don't show up in any case, please provide the log with `-v` and the rclone command and cache config.

Thanks

No, these files have been in google drive for over a year. This path doesn't have any updates so that isn't it.

I don't know how to purge the cache

```
[zenjabbamisc_cache]
type = cache
remote = zenjabbamisc:/
chunk_size = 10M
info_age = 48h
chunk_age = 12h
warmup_age = 12h
chunk_total_size = 100G
```
Deleted the cache directory, restarted the mount and they all are back.
@zenjabba I'm having the same problem, can you tell me where the directory is located?

Mine was defined from the command line, and I put it in /tmp
